paragraphs: The CineMagic Theater project is a command-line C++ application designed to simulate the experience of visiting a movie theater. Users can purchase tickets, select from a variety of snacks and beverages, and even choose their desired seats. The program utilizes data structures, arrays, and switch statements to ensure effective organization and management of user interactions. It operates entirely within the command prompt or a similar environment, offering a user-friendly and practical way to simulate a trip to the movies.
I wrote it as my final project when I was first learning to code at Guilford Technical Community College (GTCC).
features: Buy movie tickets for one of five movies at Adult ($15), Child ($10) or Senior ($7) prices.
Pick your seats from a 5 × 6 seating chart. Each movie's open seats are randomized every time the program starts.
Order concessions: snacks, food and drinks, with sub-menus for candy, popcorn, hamburgers, fountain drinks and Icees.
Get a receipt with a running total and 7% sales tax.
Print your tickets to ticket.txt, with the movie and your seats.
